A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from MN-TSG to Diff-MN, with matching authors, methods and datasets. Both complete documents, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation benchmarks, downstream forecasting, polynomial-recovery experiments, component ablations, privacy measurements and expert-weight analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and additionally reports a dense-versus-sparse MoE experiment in Table 6.

M1.justification: The main method and matched algorithms retain sample-level softmax routing, dense expert mixtures, frozen pretrained channel-wise encoding/decoding, joint diffusion generation of observations and weights, and NCDE refinement. Renaming and expanded explanations do not establish a procedural change. State-dependent routing appears in the new appendix argument but is inconsistent with the retained algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four standard generation datasets, four ECG datasets and two synthetic datasets, covering irregular-to-regular generation, continuous refinement, forecasting and polynomial recovery. The new routing comparison uses existing ECG coverage; removed visualizations do not eliminate the corresponding evaluated tasks or missingness scenarios.

E2.justification: The benchmark baseline roster is unchanged, including KO-VAE, GT-GAN, ProFITi, HeTVAE, TimeGAN, TimeVAE and diffusion. Supplementary comparisons change: v3 adds sparse MoE alternatives in Table 6, while dropping the normalized-weight alternative and the stock-refinement visual comparisons involving KO-VAE and GT-GAN.

E3.justification: New Table 6 compares dense mixtures of 1, 2, 4 or 6 experts against eight-expert sparse mixtures activating those counts, using length 24 and averaging across 30%, 50% and 70% missingness. The post-normalization control from v1 Table 9 disappears. Retained benchmark protocols are unchanged; newly identifying the forecasting model as a GRU is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: The supplementary validation changes substantially. v3 adds a dense-versus-sparse routing study addressing expert utilization under missingness, but removes v1's generated-weight positivity and sum-to-one checks, normalization sensitivity experiment, and original-versus-refined stock trajectory comparisons. Component ablations, expert-count sensitivity, expert specialization and polynomial-recovery analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 Table 7 reports cross-sample means, extrema and standard deviations of generated expert-weight sums; this descriptive dispersion report is removed in v3. This is not evidence of changed repeated-run counts. Neither version reports seed-based performance uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All matched benchmark, component-ablation, privacy and per-length tables retain their numerical entries. Changes concern supplementary results: v3 Table 6 adds dense/sparse outcomes, such as ECG5K DS of 0.269 versus 0.291 with four active experts. v1's weight-validity and normalization results, plus several stock-trajectory findings, are removed; no same-setting benchmark improvement is reported.

T1.justification: v3 drops v1's explicit continuous-and-differentiable underlying-dynamics assumption and extends the existing qualitative smoothness discussion with the mathematical argument in Appendix B.2, Equations 7–9. That argument introduces state-dependent routing unlike the retained sample-level weights, so it changes formal reasoning rather than merely notation, without establishing a consistent proof for the implemented procedure.

C1.justification: The MoE, decoupling, joint-generation and performance contributions remain. v3 adds an explicit claim to be the first formal study and evaluation of continuous TSG, and centers the contribution on diffusion-parameterized dynamics rather than compatibility with generic existing generators. The underlying demonstrated capabilities are largely retained.

C2.justification: v1's smoothness limitation is replaced by limitations concerning expert specialization under missingness, NCDE scalability, observation/interpolation dependence and evaluation on naturally irregular data. v3 adds explanations attributing dense-routing benefits to gradient stability and reduced collapse, while removing the explanation and evidence for implicitly preserving generated-weight constraints.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies Adam, learning rate 1e-3, batch size 256 and hidden dimension 64 for MoE-NCDE, and identifies the downstream predictor as a GRU. Existing diffusion architecture and training details remain. The code directory changes to Diff-MN, while the anonymous code link and explicit disclosure that generated weights are not forcibly normalized disappear.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially to GRU-D, ODE-RNN/Latent ODE, TrajGPT, CTFP and recent targeted, causal and text-controlled diffusion work. ProFITi is now described as a conditional-flow method rather than grouped with attention approaches. This broader discussion accompanies the explicit first-study claim and revised diffusion-centered positioning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and method narrative, renames the framework and introduces SIN/RN terminology. It separates limitations from the conclusion and reorganizes the appendix into related work, NCDE discussion, algorithms, settings and results, replacing much of the earlier extended discussion with compact cross-references.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive relocation and resizing of displays. Figure 2 is reorganized and relabeled, Figure 7 gains clearer axes, and numerous captions are revised. A dense/sparse table is added, while weight-validation tables and normalization/refinement figures are removed; most surviving experimental plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, discloses useful implementation settings and adds routing comparisons and practical limitations. However, it removes validation of diffusion-generated weights and baseline refinement case studies. Its new Appendix B.2 argument also uses state-dependent routing inconsistent with the retained method and does not establish nonsmoothness merely from rapid variation. These substantive gains and losses leave the net quality change uncertain.
